name: Dehumidifiers
hub_intro: Ireland's damp climate makes dehumidifiers less a luxury than a household appliance category of their own: condensation on windows, mould creeping into corners, laundry that takes two days to dry indoors. The right machine fixes all three for cents per day. We compare compressor and desiccant models across every budget and room size, with running costs at Irish electricity rates.
guide: Compressor models are cheaper to run and ideal for typical Irish indoor temps (15–25°C). Desiccant models work better in cold spaces — garages, unheated rooms under 15°C — but use roughly double the electricity. Most homes want a compressor unit.

The headline number (10L, 12L, 20L) is extraction per day under test conditions. Rule of thumb: 10–12L for apartments and bedrooms, 20L for a 3-bed house with drying laundry, 25L+ for big or very damp homes.

A modern 12L compressor unit draws ~160 W: about 5–6 cents per hour. Run 8 hours daily and you spend roughly €12–15 a month — usually less than the heating energy wasted evaporating damp air, which is why a dehumidifier can lower total bills.
Laundry mode is the killer feature

If you dry clothes indoors (most of Ireland, most of the year), laundry mode pays for the machine: a good unit dries a load overnight for ~6 cents of electricity versus ~€1.50+ per tumble-dryer cycle, and without the condensation hitting your walls.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for an Irish home?
faqs.a: Apartments and single rooms: 10–12L/day. Standard 3-bed semi: 20L. Large, old or very damp houses: 25L+. Oversizing slightly is fine — bigger units hit target humidity faster and then idle, which is actually more efficient.

faqs.q: How much does a dehumidifier cost to run in Ireland?
faqs.a: A 12L compressor model at ~160 W costs about 5–6 cents per hour at typical rates. Eight hours a day works out around €12–15 per month. Desiccant models cost roughly double — but heat the room as a side effect.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier stop mould and condensation?
faqs.a: Yes, if you keep relative humidity under 60%. Mould cannot establish below that level. Run the unit on auto with a 50–55% target, keep furniture slightly off cold external walls, and wipe existing mould once with a fungicidal cleaner.

faqs.q: Can I dry clothes with a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Absolutely — it's the cheapest indoor drying method in Ireland. Put the airer in a small closed room with the unit on laundry mode and a typical load dries in 6–10 hours for under 10 cents, with no window condensation.

faqs.q: Dehumidifier or PIV system for a damp house?
faqs.a: A dehumidifier is the fast, no-install fix and handles most condensation damp. PIV (positive input ventilation) suits whole-house problems but needs attic installation and ~€800–1,200 fitted. Start with a €200 dehumidifier; escalate only if damp persists.

faqs.q: Where should I place a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Centrally, doors open, for whole-floor drying — or in the problem room with the door shut for targeted work. Keep 20 cm clearance around intakes. For laundry, small closed room beats hallway every time.

Compressor models run 38–48 dB — quiet fan to gentle hum. For bedrooms pick a unit with a night mode under 40 dB, or run it daytime only; a few hours daily is enough for most rooms once humidity is under control.

faqs.q: Why is my house so damp in winter?
faqs.a: Cold external walls + sealed windows + indoor moisture (cooking, showers, breathing, drying clothes adds ~10L/day for a family) = condensation. Modern retrofits make houses airtight without adding ventilation. A dehumidifier removes that moisture before it hits the glass.

pages.title: 5 Best Dehumidifiers in Ireland 2026 — Tested for Damp Irish Homes
pages.desc: Ireland's best dehumidifiers compared: extraction, running costs at Irish electricity rates, noise and laundry drying. Top 5 for 2026.
pages.intro: We compared the dehumidifiers Irish households actually buy — on extraction rates, electricity cost per litre removed, noise, and how fast they dry a winter washing load. The five below cover every budget from €160 to €330. One spoiler: the brand that dominates this market (Meaco) earns its position, but it isn't the right answer for every room.

products.name: MeacoDry Arete One 12L
pros: Quietest compressor unit in its class
HEPA filter doubles as air purifier
5-year warranty — unheard of in this market
cons: 2.5 L tank needs daily emptying when very damp
Laundry mode is timed, not sensor-driven
products.verdict: The Irish bestseller for good reason: near-silent, sips electricity, five-year warranty. For a typical 2–3 bed home this is the default answer.

products.name: Meaco Low Energy 20L
pros: Dries a full washing load overnight
cons: Bulkier and louder than the Arete
products.verdict: For big, busy or properly damp houses: twice the extraction, a tank you rarely empty, and the lowest cost per litre of water removed we've calculated.

products.name: Pro Breeze 12L
pros: Compact, easy to move room to room
products.verdict: Eighty-five percent of the Meaco experience at three-quarters of the price. If the budget is firm, this is where value peaks.

products.name: EcoAir DD1 Simple MK3 (Desiccant)
pros: Gently warms the room as it works
products.verdict: The cold-space specialist: garages, unheated bedrooms, holiday homes left empty. Where compressor units stall, the DD1 keeps pulling water.

products.name: ElectriQ CD12PRO-LE
pros: UV-C and ioniser for mould-prone homes
products.verdict: For data lovers and mould fighters: track room humidity from your phone and add UV air treatment. A geekier alternative to the Pro Breeze at similar money.

pages.title: Best Small Dehumidifiers for Bedrooms & Apartments Ireland 2026
pages.desc: Quiet, compact dehumidifiers for Irish bedrooms, apartments and single rooms — noise levels, size and running costs compared. Top 5 picks.
pages.h1: Best Small & Bedroom Dehumidifiers in Ireland
pages.intro: Condensation hits bedrooms hardest — we each breathe out half a litre of moisture a night into a cold, closed room. The fix needs to be small enough for a corner and quiet enough to sleep beside. We ranked these five on noise first, then extraction and footprint, because a dehumidifier you switch off at bedtime is a dehumidifier that doesn't work.

products.name: MeacoDry Arete One 10L
cons: Premium price for a small unit
products.verdict: The bedroom benchmark. Most 'quiet' units mean quiet-ish; the Arete's night mode is library-level, and it still clears morning window mist by breakfast.

products.name: Pro Breeze 500ml Mini
cons: Only suits mild damp in small rooms
products.verdict: Know its limits and it delights: a box room, ensuite or wardrobe with light condensation. It will not fix a properly damp room — buy the Arete for that.

products.name: EcoAir DD1 Simple MK3
products.verdict: The quiet alternative with real pulling power, especially in bedrooms that run cold. Use it on a timer to manage the higher wattage.

products.name: Russell Hobbs RHDH1101
cons: 43 dB — daytime use, light sleepers beware
products.verdict: The price-performance pick for daytime use: run it while at work, come home to dry air. Light sleepers should pay up for the Meaco.

products.name: Duux Bora Smart 20L
pros: Actually attractive in a living space
App scheduling around night rate electricity
products.verdict: For studio and open-plan apartments where the machine lives in view: Scandinavian looks, app smarts and enough power for the whole space.

pages.title: Best 20L+ Dehumidifiers for Large & Damp Homes Ireland 2026
pages.desc: Big-capacity 20–25L dehumidifiers for large or very damp Irish houses — extraction, continuous drainage and efficiency compared. Top 5.
pages.h1: Best 20L+ Dehumidifiers for Large Irish Homes
pages.intro: Older Irish housing stock — solid walls, single glazing, suspect ventilation — can produce damp faster than small machines remove it. For 4+ bedrooms, persistent mould or post-leak drying, you want 20–25L of daily extraction, a big tank or hose drainage, and efficiency that doesn't punish all-day running. These five are the heavy lifters.

products.name: Meaco Low Energy 25L
pros: Drinks moisture from whole floors at once
Best efficiency per litre in the big class
products.verdict: When damp is a battle, bring artillery. Hose it to a drain, set 50%, and entire floors of a damp house dry out and stay dry.

products.name: Meaco Low Energy 20L
pros: The sweet spot of the heavy class
products.verdict: The standard prescription for a damp 4-bed semi: enough extraction to win, efficiency to run daily, and Meaco's support behind it.

products.name: ElectriQ CD25PRO-LE-V2
products.verdict: Maximum litres per euro in the big class. The small tank assumes hose drainage — plan for that and it's a bargain workhorse.

products.name: Pro Breeze 20L Premium
products.verdict: The budget path to serious extraction. Slightly more electricity per litre than the Meaco — but €100 buys years of that difference.

products.name: Inventor Eva Ion Pro 20L
pros: Ioniser helps with musty damp smell
Swing louvre spreads dry air further
products.verdict: For homes where damp brought its friend — that musty smell. Solid 20L extraction plus active air treatment at a fair price.

pages.title: Best Dehumidifiers for Drying Clothes Indoors Ireland 2026
pages.desc: Dry washing indoors overnight for cents: the 5 best laundry-mode dehumidifiers in Ireland vs tumble dryer costs. Compared 2026.
pages.h1: Best Dehumidifiers for Drying Clothes in Ireland
pages.intro: Eight months a year, the Irish washing line is theoretical. A tumble dryer costs roughly €1.30–1.80 per load at current rates; a dehumidifier in laundry mode dries the same load overnight for about 6–10 cents — gentler on clothes, with zero condensation soaking your walls. These five have the strongest dedicated laundry performance we compared.

products.name: Meaco Low Energy 20L (Laundry)
pros: Full family load dry by morning
Tank swallows multiple loads of water
cons: Needs a smallish closed room to excel
products.verdict: The tumble-dryer replacement. Six months of family laundry pays the price difference versus running a dryer — then it keeps saving for years.

products.name: MeacoDry Arete One 12L (Laundry)
pros: Quiet enough to dry overnight near bedrooms
Doubles as the home's main unit
products.verdict: For one-to-two-person households: overnight drying without the noise, from the machine you'd buy anyway for general damp.

products.name: EcoAir DD1 Simple MK3 (Laundry)
pros: Adds gentle warmth that speeds drying
products.verdict: If your drying space is an unheated utility room or garage — where compressor units sulk — the desiccant DD1 is the only right answer.

products.name: Pro Breeze 20L Premium (Laundry)
cons: A touch slower than the Meaco 20L
products.verdict: The budget family choice: handles full loads overnight at ~10 cents each. The Meaco does it slightly better; this does it for €100 less.

products.name: Vax Power Extract 18L
products.verdict: A dependable all-rounder whose laundry boost punches above its price — worth grabbing whenever it dips under €180.

pages.title: Best Dehumidifiers for Mould & Serious Damp Ireland 2026
pages.desc: Fighting black mould or persistent damp in an Irish home? The 5 best dehumidifiers with HEPA/UV air treatment and high extraction, compared.
pages.h1: Best Dehumidifiers for Mould & Serious Damp in Ireland
pages.intro: Black mould on walls is a humidity problem wearing a scary costume: keep a room under 60% RH and mould physically cannot grow. For homes already showing spots — window reveals, cold corners, behind wardrobes — you want strong extraction plus air filtration to catch spores. These five pair the muscle with the filters, ranked by how fast they make mould's life impossible.

products.name: MeacoDry Arete One 20L
cons: Tank smaller than Low Energy line
products.verdict: The complete anti-mould system: starves mould of moisture while HEPA-filtering the spores already airborne. The one we'd put in a mouldy rental tomorrow.

products.name: ElectriQ CD20PRO-LE-V2 (UV)
pros: Aggressive price for the feature set
products.verdict: The tech-forward mould fighter: extraction, UV and data logging let you watch the room drop below the mould threshold and stay there.

products.name: Meaco Low Energy 25L (Damp Rescue)
cons: No HEPA — pair with cleaning spray
products.verdict: For rising/penetrating damp, post-leak recovery or a house that's been empty: maximum water removal first, refinement later.

products.name: Pro Breeze 12L Compressor (Starter)
pros: Gets a single mouldy room under control
products.verdict: The minimum effective dose: one problem bedroom or bathroom corner, €169, sorted. Whole-house damp needs the bigger artillery above.

products.name: Ionmax ION632 Desiccant
pros: Full power in cold north-facing rooms
products.verdict: Mould loves cold rooms; compressors don't. For the unheated north-facing bedroom with spots on the ceiling, this desiccant keeps extracting where others quit.
